Satisfied Iyer takes positives from New Zealand series win

India's preparation is on track for next year's Cricket World Cup, according to skipper Shreyas Iyer.

15 November, 2026
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:37
Instaread

India captain Shreyas Iyer has taken plenty of positives from his side's hard-fought ODI series victory over New Zealand.

The five-match ODI series in New Zealand came to an end in Mount Maunganui on Sunday, with India recording a narrow 22-run triumph in the final fixture to clinch a 3-1 scoreline in their favour.

There were plenty of ups and downs for India across the series, with the performance of their bowling unit a clear standout less than 12 month out from the next edition of the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup when Iyer's side will attempt to go one better than their runner-up finish behind Australia on home soil in 2023.

While Iyer admitted the conditions his team faced in New Zealand will be vastly different to what they will encounter in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia at the World Cup next year, the India captain said it was a good challenge for his players to adapt their game to the different game situations they faced.

"We are in New Zealand, so we can't really compare with South Africa. Weather will be different. Especially from the batting point of view, both teams, it did not happen, our bowling was consistently good and theirs too, and the wicket was predominantly bowler support," Iyer said.

"But the most important thing for us was to win the series, and we won. So after that, we don't think much about the rest.

"Definitely, there will be takeaways. Every individual will reflect within themselves, and we have been playing for a long time, so mentally you get exhausted the longer series you play. So adaptability also, on every wicket it's different, there is a challenge, but keep learning and definitely you accept the challenge and move on."

Being bowled out for just 89 in the fourth ODI was the clear negative for India across the white-ball portion of the New Zealand series, but Iyer said his team moved on quickly from the disappointment.

"Both the series T20 and ODI coming over here, we were provided with different conditions. The weather kept changing. Faced a lot of challenges and coming out triumphant, it's a great achievement. And today we had that certain kind of belief even though we didn't get that many runs in batting. But still we were hoping that we can change the game at any point of time," he said.

"And I'm glad that every individual thought in the same direction and we were able to execute that."

Every Shreyas Iyer Boundary | Champions Trophy 2025

While disappointed his side lost the series, New Zealand skipper Mitchell Santner said his team also took a lot of positives from the series.

"You look at the scoreline, 3-1, and I think it was closer than that. We played some good cricket. Obviously, there was a bit of rain around and we lost a few tosses. But in between all that, there were a lot of positives," Santner said.

"Even today and in the previous game, if we had taken things a little deeper, there was enough time in 50-over cricket. Different guys got opportunities, and it was good experience. A number of players stepped up as well, which was nice."

India v New Zealand ODI series:

First ODI: November 4, Auckland [India won by 5 wickets (DLS method)]

Second ODI: November 7, Wellington [India won by Four Runs (DLS Method)]

Third ODI: November 10, Hamilton [No result]

Fourth ODI: November 13, Mount Maunganui [New Zealand won by 244 runs]

Fifth ODI: November 15, Mount Maunganui (India won by 22 runs)
